summary: The note describes a set of art and cultural exchange projects run by local schools that pair students with peers abroad to build empathy and intercultural understanding. Projects span visual art, crafts, music, textiles, oral histories and a virtual showcase, each led by a named educator and launched between September and December 2023. The note argues these exchanges foster cultural understanding, friendships and global citizenship.
one_line: Local schools launched art, music, textile, oral-history and online exhibition exchange projects in 2023 to connect students across countries and build cultural empathy.
key_facts: "Canvas Connect" launched on September 15, 2023, led by art educator Eleanor Vasquez of Lincoln High School.

In Canvas Connect, students sketch their community, dreams or cultural heritage in a shared sketchbook and send it to a partner school abroad; partners include schools in Kyoto, Japan and São Paulo, Brazil.
The "Embracing Differences" initiative began on November 1, 2023, organized by cultural education specialist Marcus Leung.
Embracing Differences uses video conferences and hands-on workshops so students discuss and recreate traditional arts and crafts of partner schools' cultures.
The Harmony Without Borders initiative debuted on September 21, 2023, the international Day of Peace, under music instructor Clara Rodriguez.
Students at Patterson Secondary School exchange music pieces and watch streamed virtual concerts with a school in Cairo, Egypt.
The Tapestry of Cultures project emerged in mid-October 2023, created by fashion educator Helena Choi, with students trading textile and pattern samples that symbolize their cultural identity.
The long-term goal of Tapestry of Cultures is an enormous patchwork tapestry with contributions from each participating school.
"The Living Library" launched in late September 2023 under history teacher Jacob Edwards; students interview community elders and share oral histories and folklore with peers abroad.
The Global Gallery, a virtual exhibition of student artwork, performances and narratives, launched on December 10, 2023.
The Global Gallery is curated by a team of educators and art enthusiasts and serves as a community for feedback, discussion and planning future collaborations.
The note says the projects have produced growth in students' cultural understanding and empathy and long-lasting friendships.
